l6hu-tourney: HU Tournaments: The Game of Chips and Blinds

HU tournaments (SNG final table / MTT heads-up) differ from ante-structure, fixed-depth cash games: blinds rise over time, chips are a finite resource, and ICM pressure dominates decisions. In HU tournaments, chip rhythm becomes the core — deep stacks (40BB+) can maintain cash-style postflop play, while shallow stacks (under 20BB) shift to preflop shove games.

The golden rule of HU tournaments: the shallower the stack and the higher the blind share, the more frequent preflop shoves. ICM and blind pressure make "survival" and "aggression" equally important goals.

The ICM at an HU SNG final table is simple: the winner takes all the prize, so ICM pressure is lower than full ring but still affects decisions — you avoid unnecessary variance when deep (protecting the lead) and use high aggression to double when behind. Blind attack/defense: shallow-stacked (like 15-20BB), the min-raise steal + shove becomes the main weapon because rising blinds make your steals auto-profit; while cash's complex postflop play fails at shallow stacks.

Example: HU SNG final table, you have 18BB vs the opponent's 22BB, blinds 0.5/1. You (SB) hold A♠4♠. At this depth, A4s is in the standard push/shove range: about 50% equity vs the BB's ~60% calling range, the 18BB shove is +EV, and rising blinds lower the value of waiting. Deep-stacked (60BB+), A4s is still an open but with more postflop room. Stack depth directly changes how the same hand plays.

Example 2 (the urgency of rising blinds): HU MTT final, blinds rise every 5 minutes and you drop from 30BB to 12BB. Now "waiting for good cards" is wrong — rising blinds spike your waiting cost. The correct strategy is raising shove frequency, using any hand with equity (pairs, Ax, strong suited connectors) to steal and double. The key to chip rhythm: act before the blinds devour you.

Counterintuitive point: the ICM logic of "conservative when ahead, aggressive when behind" in HU tournaments differs from cash's "always max EV". When deep and ahead, avoid big variance; when behind, double aggressively — because in a tournament only first place matters.

HU tournament chip-rhythm quick memory: (1) 40BB+ deep stacks maintain cash-style play; (2) 20-40BB medium stacks, min-raise + postflop; (3) under 15BB shallow stacks, shoves dominate. Re-evaluate your strategy after every blind rise — don't let the old rhythm hurt you.

l6hu-tourney-q1.question: The core difference between HU tournaments and cash is:
options: Blinds rise, chips are finite, ICM pressure dominates
l6hu-tourney-q1.explanation: HU tournaments have rising blinds, finite chips, and ICM pressure, with strategy adjusting dynamically by stack depth.

l6hu-tourney-q2.question: The correct strategy at HU tournament shallow stacks (under 15BB) is:
options: Preflop shoves dominate, stealing with any hand with equity
l6hu-tourney-q2.explanation: At shallow stacks preflop shoves become the main weapon because rising blinds make steals auto-profit and waiting costs spike.

l6hu-tourney-q3.question: The ICM characteristic of an HU SNG final table is:
options: Extremely high ICM pressure, near full ring
The winner takes all; ICM pressure is relatively low but still affects decisions
ICM only exists on the bubble
l6hu-tourney-q3.explanation: The HU final-table winner takes all, so ICM pressure is relatively low vs full ring but still affects decisions — avoid variance when deep, double aggressively when behind.

l6hu-tourney-q4.question: The effect of rising blinds on HU tournament strategy is:
options: Waiting costs spike — raise action frequency rather than waiting for cards
l6hu-tourney-q4.explanation: Rising blinds spike your waiting cost; the correct strategy is raising shove/steal frequency and acting before the blinds devour you.

l6hu-tourney-q5.question: The strategy at the 20-40BB medium-stack stage of HU tournaments is:
options: Min-raise + postflop, balancing steal and postflop
l6hu-tourney-q5.explanation: The medium stage (20-40BB) balances steal and postflop — min-raise plus postflop is reasonable, differing from the shallow-stack shove-dominant approach.
